# Tidymodels bridge for greedy CI trees

This flat file registers `ineqTrees` as a parsnip engine for
`decision_tree()` and `rand_forest()`, and exposes a yardstick-compatible
concentration-index gain metric.

Assessment gain applies the fitted partition to held-out observations and
compares its weighted within-leaf impurity with the unsplit assessment
sample. Training gain makes the same comparison on the analysis sample
used to fit that model. Ranks are recomputed within each scored leaf for
the rank-dependent criteria. Forest gain averages these partition gains
over member trees.

Predicted risk alone cannot identify the partition: two leaves can have
the same mean, and averaged forest predictions combine several partitions.
The engine therefore retains terminal-node IDs alongside `.pred`. It also
caches the analysis-sample assignments used for training diagnostics in
`attr(engine, "ci_training_diagnostics")`. These assignments matter when
partykit routes a factor level absent from a member's training sample
probabilistically. A fresh prediction can make a different routing draw;
the saved metadata identifies the draw actually scored.

## Tune on assessment gain and inspect training gain

The example uses synthetic child-level observations with complete data and
unequal importance weights. Zero-weight observations, when present, do not
contribute to impurity calculations. Include the socioeconomic variable in
the workflow inputs so the engine can recover it. The bridge removes it
from the splitting predictors in the single-outcome interface. Recipes must
retain the rank/level variable and the case-weight role. Do not transform
the socioeconomic levels when using L unless that transformation is part
of the intended estimand.

```{r bridge-tuning-example}
example_data <- data.frame(
  rank = seq_len(48),
  outcome = as.numeric(seq_len(48) %% 7 == 0 | seq_len(48) > 28),
  group = rep(seq_len(6), each = 8),
  weight = rep(c(1, 2, 3), 16)
)
example_data$case_wt <- hardhat::importance_weights(example_data$weight)

tree_spec <- parsnip::decision_tree(
  tree_depth = tune::tune(),
  min_n = 2
)
tree_spec <- parsnip::set_engine(
  tree_spec,
  "ineqTrees",
  rank_name = "rank",
  outcome_name = "outcome",
  type = "CI",
  minsplit = 4,
  minprob = 0
)
tree_spec <- parsnip::set_mode(tree_spec, "regression")

tree_workflow <- workflows::workflow()
tree_workflow <- workflows::add_model(tree_workflow, tree_spec)
tree_workflow <- workflows::add_formula(
  tree_workflow, outcome ~ rank + group
)
tree_workflow <- workflows::add_case_weights(tree_workflow, case_wt)

set.seed(71)
example_folds <- rsample::vfold_cv(example_data, v = 3)
gain_metrics <- ci_tuning_metric_set(
  example_data,
  rank_name = "rank",
  case_weight_name = "weight",
  type = "CI",
  metrics = c(
    "validation_gain", "relative_validation_gain",
    "training_gain", "relative_training_gain"
  )
)
tree_tuning <- tune::tune_grid(
  tree_workflow,
  resamples = example_folds,
  grid = data.frame(tree_depth = c(1L, 2L)),
  metrics = gain_metrics,
  control = tune::control_grid(save_pred = TRUE, allow_par = FALSE)
)

tune::collect_metrics(tree_tuning)
tune::select_best(tree_tuning, metric = "validation_gain")
```

Relative training gain uses the analysis root as its denominator; relative
validation gain uses the assessment root. Either relative gain is undefined
when its root impurity is numerically zero and is reported as `NA`.
Use validation gain for selection. Training gain describes the fitted
sample and helps reveal a training-validation gap. It does not establish
generalisation or a causal effect. Keep the metric's `type` consistent with
the engine, and compare tuning candidates within the same criterion.

For reproducible numerical checks, run
`/usr/bin/Rscript dev/run_tidymodels_scoring_experiments.R` from the package
root. The script checks actual node assignments against an independent
weighted calculation and saves fold scores, selection checks and versions
under `dev/validation/tidymodels_scoring/`.

```{r, function-tidymodels_bridge}
utils::globalVariables(c("object", "new_data"))

#' Convert parsnip formulas to the two-column CI response
#'
#' @noRd
.ci_parsnip_formula <- function(formula, data, rank_name, outcome_name) {
  response_vars <- all.vars(formula[[2L]])
  response_call <- formula[[2L]]
  is_ci_response <- is.call(response_call) &&
    identical(as.character(response_call[[1L]]), "cbind") &&
    length(response_vars) >= 2L

  if (is_ci_response) {
    return(list(formula = formula, outcome_name = outcome_name))
  }

  if (!rank_name %in% names(data)) {
    stop("`data` must contain `rank_name` when using a single-outcome formula.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  actual_outcome_name <- outcome_name
  if (!actual_outcome_name %in% names(data) &&
      length(response_vars) &&
      response_vars[[1L]] %in% names(data)) {
    actual_outcome_name <- response_vars[[1L]]
  }
  if (!actual_outcome_name %in% names(data)) {
    stop(
      "`data` must contain `outcome_name` when using a single-outcome formula.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  term_labels <- attr(stats::terms(formula, data = data), "term.labels")
  if (identical(term_labels, ".")) {
    predictor_names <- names(data)
  } else {
    predictor_names <- term_labels
  }
  predictor_names <- setdiff(
    predictor_names,
    c(rank_name, outcome_name, actual_outcome_name)
  )
  if (!length(predictor_names)) {
    stop("`formula` must contain at least one predictor besides `rank_name`.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  rhs <- paste(predictor_names, collapse = " + ")
  formula <- stats::as.formula(
    paste0("cbind(", rank_name, ", ", outcome_name, ") ~ ", rhs),
    env = environment(formula)
  )
  if (!identical(actual_outcome_name, outcome_name)) {
    formula <- stats::as.formula(
      paste0("cbind(", rank_name, ", ", actual_outcome_name, ") ~ ", rhs),
      env = environment(formula)
    )
  }

  list(formula = formula, outcome_name = actual_outcome_name)
}

#' Fit a greedy CI tree from parsnip
#'
#' @description
#' A small wrapper used by the `ineqTrees` parsnip engine for
#' `parsnip::decision_tree()`. The formula can be either the native
#' `cbind(rank, outcome) ~ predictors` response or the usual tidymodels
#' `outcome ~ predictors` response when `rank_name` and `outcome_name` are
#' supplied through `set_engine()`.
#'
#' @param formula A model formula, typically
#'   `cbind(rank, outcome) ~ predictors`.
#' @param data A data frame containing the variables in `formula`.
#' @param weights Optional case weights supplied by parsnip/hardhat.
#' @param rank_name Name of the socioeconomic rank variable.
#' @param outcome_name Name of the outcome variable.
#' @param type One of `"CI"`, `"CIg"`, `"CIc"`, or `"L"`.
#' @param tree_depth Optional parsnip tree-depth value.
#' @param minbucket Minimum weighted child-node size.
#' @param minsplit Minimum weighted parent-node size.
#' @param minprob Minimum child-node weight proportion.
#' @param maxdepth Maximum tree depth. When supplied through `set_engine()`,
#'   this overrides `tree_depth`.
#' @param min_gain Minimum concentration-index gain required to split.
#' @param min_relative_gain Minimum concentration-index gain as a share of the
#'   parent-node impurity required to split.
#' @param na.action Function for handling missing values.
#' @param ... Additional arguments passed to [ci_tree()].
#'
#' @return A fitted `ci_tree` object.
#'
#' @export
ci_tree_parsnip <- function(formula,
                            data,
                            weights = NULL,
                            rank_name = "wealth",
                            outcome_name = "deadu5_num",
                            type = "CIg",
                            tree_depth = NULL,
                            minbucket = 100L,
                            minsplit = 200L,
                            minprob = 0.01,
                            maxdepth = 4L,
                            min_gain = 0,
                            min_relative_gain = 0,
                            na.action = stats::na.omit,
                            ...) {
  if (!is.null(weights)) {
    weights <- as.numeric(weights)
  }

  if (!missing(maxdepth)) {
    depth <- maxdepth
  } else if (!is.null(tree_depth)) {
    depth <- tree_depth
  } else {
    depth <- maxdepth
  }

  control <- ci_tree_control(
    minsplit = as.integer(minsplit),
    minbucket = as.integer(minbucket),
    minprob = minprob,
    maxdepth = as.integer(depth),
    min_gain = min_gain,
    min_relative_gain = min_relative_gain
  )

  prepared <- .ci_parsnip_formula(
    formula = formula,
    data = data,
    rank_name = rank_name,
    outcome_name = outcome_name
  )
  formula <- prepared$formula
  outcome_name <- prepared$outcome_name

  fit <- ci_tree(
    formula = formula,
    data = data,
    rank_name = rank_name,
    outcome_name = outcome_name,
    weights = weights,
    type = type,
    control = control,
    na.action = na.action,
    ...
  )

  attr(fit, "ci_training_diagnostics") <- .ci_parsnip_training_scores(fit)
  fit
}
```

```{r, function-ci_forest_parsnip}
#' Fit a greedy CI forest from parsnip
#'
#' @description
#' A small wrapper used by the `ineqTrees` parsnip engine for
#' `parsnip::rand_forest()`.
#'
#' @inheritParams ci_tree_parsnip
#' @param ntree Number of trees to grow.
#' @param mtry Optional number of variables tried at each split.
#' @param perturb Resampling specification passed to [ci_forest()].
#'
#' @return A fitted `ci_forest` object.
#'
#' @export
ci_forest_parsnip <- function(formula,
                              data,
                              weights = NULL,
                              rank_name = "wealth",
                              outcome_name = "deadu5_num",
                              type = "CIg",
                              ntree = 500L,
                              mtry = NULL,
                              minbucket = 100L,
                              minsplit = 200L,
                              minprob = 0.01,
                              maxdepth = 4L,
                              min_gain = 0,
                              min_relative_gain = 0,
                              perturb = list(replace = FALSE, fraction = 0.632),
                              na.action = stats::na.omit,
                              ...) {
  if (!is.null(weights)) {
    weights <- as.numeric(weights)
  }

  control <- ci_tree_control(
    minsplit = as.integer(minsplit),
    minbucket = as.integer(minbucket),
    minprob = minprob,
    maxdepth = as.integer(maxdepth),
    min_gain = min_gain,
    min_relative_gain = min_relative_gain
  )

  prepared <- .ci_parsnip_formula(
    formula = formula,
    data = data,
    rank_name = rank_name,
    outcome_name = outcome_name
  )
  formula <- prepared$formula
  outcome_name <- prepared$outcome_name

  fit <- ci_forest(
    formula = formula,
    data = data,
    rank_name = rank_name,
    outcome_name = outcome_name,
    weights = weights,
    type = type,
    control = control,
    ntree = as.integer(ntree),
    mtry = mtry,
    perturb = perturb,
    na.action = na.action,
    ...
  )

  attr(fit, "ci_training_diagnostics") <- .ci_parsnip_training_scores(fit)
  fit
}
```

```{r, function-ci_predict_parsnip}
#' Predict risks and retain CI partitions for tidymodels scoring
#'
#' @description
#' The numeric prediction method used by the `ineqTrees` parsnip engines.
#' Keeps `.pred` as the predicted outcome and adds `.ci_node`, `.ci_type`,
#' `.ci_training_gain`, and `.ci_training_root` for [ci_tuning_metric_set()].
#' Tree node IDs are integers. Forest node IDs are a list of integer vectors,
#' with one entry per member tree for each observation.
#'
#' Training diagnostics use the fitted analysis sample. Forest gains average
#' the gains of member-tree partitions applied to that whole analysis sample,
#' rather than scoring each member's bootstrap sample separately.
#' Risk predictions use the same node assignments as the scoring metadata.
#' Factor levels absent from a member's sample retain partykit's probabilistic
#' routing behaviour. Saved predictions identify the assignments actually used.
#'
#' @param object A fitted `ci_tree` or `ci_forest` engine object.
#' @param newdata Data containing the predictors required by the fitted model.
#'
#' @return A tibble with predictions and partition-scoring metadata.
#' @export
ci_predict_parsnip <- function(object, newdata) {
  if (!inherits(object, "ci_tree") && !inherits(object, "ci_forest")) {
    stop("`object` must be a fitted CI tree or forest.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  nodes <- stats::predict(object, newdata = newdata, type = "node")
  if (is.matrix(nodes)) {
    member_predictions <- vapply(seq_along(object$trees), function(member) {
      as.numeric(partykit::predict_party(
        object$trees[[member]]$fit,
        id = as.integer(nodes[, member]),
        type = "response"
      ))
    }, numeric(nrow(newdata)))
    prediction <- rowMeans(matrix(
      member_predictions,
      nrow = nrow(newdata),
      ncol = length(object$trees)
    ))
    nodes <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(nodes)), function(i) {
      as.integer(nodes[i, ])
    })
  } else {
    nodes <- as.integer(nodes)
    prediction <- as.numeric(partykit::predict_party(
      object, id = nodes, type = "response"
    ))
  }

  training <- attr(object, "ci_training_diagnostics", exact = TRUE)
  if (is.null(training)) {
    training <- .ci_parsnip_training_scores(object)
  }

  tibble::tibble(
    .pred = prediction,
    .ci_node = nodes,
    .ci_type = training$type,
    .ci_training_gain = training$gain,
    .ci_training_root = training$root
  )
}

#' Compute analysis-sample diagnostics once when the parsnip model is fitted
#' @noRd
.ci_parsnip_training_scores <- function(fit) {
  if (inherits(fit, "ci_forest")) {
    type <- fit$type
    rank <- fit$data[[fit$rank_name]]
    outcome <- fit$data[[fit$outcome_name]]
    weights <- fit$weights
    node_matrix <- stats::predict(fit, type = "node")
    nodes <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(node_matrix)), function(i) {
      as.integer(node_matrix[i, ])
    })
  } else {
    type <- fit$info$type
    response <- stats::model.response(fit$data)
    rank <- response[, 1L]
    outcome <- response[, 2L]
    weights <- fit$fitted[["(weights)"]]
    nodes <- fit$fitted[["(fitted)"]]
  }

  root <- ci_factory(type)(cbind(rank, outcome), weights)
  gain <- .ci_tuning_partition_gain(
    truth = outcome,
    estimate = outcome,
    vectors = list(rank = rank, weights = weights, node = nodes),
    type = type,
    root_impurity = NULL,
    na_rm = TRUE
  )
  list(type = type, gain = gain, root = root, nodes = nodes)
}
```

```{r, function-register_ineqtrees_parsnip}
#' Replace this package's prediction entry when reloading development code
#' @noRd
.ci_register_prediction <- function(model, type, value) {
  registry_name <- paste0(model, "_predict")
  registered <- parsnip::get_from_env(registry_name)
  replace_rows <- registered$engine %in% "ineqTrees" &
    registered$mode %in% "regression" & registered$type %in% type

  # Parsnip rejects changed prediction definitions. Its registry survives
  # pkgload reloads, so remove only our matching entry before registering it.
  registration_complete <- FALSE
  on.exit({
    if (!registration_complete) {
      parsnip::set_env_val(registry_name, registered)
    }
  }, add = TRUE)

  parsnip::set_env_val(
    registry_name, registered[!replace_rows, , drop = FALSE]
  )
  parsnip::set_pred(
    model = model,
    mode = "regression",
    eng = "ineqTrees",
    type = type,
    value = value
  )
  registration_complete <- TRUE
  invisible(TRUE)
}

#' Register `ineqTrees` parsnip engines
#'
#' @description
#' Registers `ineqTrees` as a regression engine for
#' `parsnip::decision_tree()` and `parsnip::rand_forest()`.
#' Refreshes this package's prediction entries when development code is
#' reloaded in the same R session, preserving other engines' registrations.
#'
#' @return Invisibly, `TRUE`.
#'
#' @examples
#' if (requireNamespace("parsnip", quietly = TRUE)) {
#'   register_ineqtrees_parsnip()
#' }
#'
#' @export
register_ineqtrees_parsnip <- function() {
  register_ineqtrees_decision_tree()
  register_ineqtrees_rand_forest()
  invisible(TRUE)
}

#' Register the `decision_tree()` `ineqTrees` engine
#'
#' @return Invisibly, `TRUE`.
#'
#' @export
register_ineqtrees_decision_tree <- function() {
  if (!any(parsnip::show_engines("decision_tree")$engine == "ineqTrees")) {
    parsnip::set_model_engine(
      model = "decision_tree",
      mode = "regression",
      eng = "ineqTrees"
    )
  }

  parsnip::set_dependency("decision_tree", eng = "ineqTrees", pkg = "ineqTrees")

  parsnip::set_model_arg(
    model = "decision_tree",
    eng = "ineqTrees",
    parsnip = "tree_depth",
    original = "tree_depth",
    func = list(pkg = "dials", fun = "tree_depth"),
    has_submodel = FALSE
  )

  parsnip::set_model_arg(
    model = "decision_tree",
    eng = "ineqTrees",
    parsnip = "min_n",
    original = "minbucket",
    func = list(pkg = "dials", fun = "min_n"),
    has_submodel = FALSE
  )

  parsnip::set_encoding(
    model = "decision_tree",
    mode = "regression",
    eng = "ineqTrees",
    options = list(
      predictor_indicators = "none",
      compute_intercept = FALSE,
      remove_intercept = FALSE,
      allow_sparse_x = FALSE
    )
  )

  parsnip::set_fit(
    model = "decision_tree",
    mode = "regression",
    eng = "ineqTrees",
    value = list(
      interface = "formula",
      data = c(formula = "formula", data = "data", weights = "weights"),
      protect = c("formula", "data", "weights"),
      func = c(pkg = "ineqTrees", fun = "ci_tree_parsnip"),
      defaults = list()
    )
  )

  .ci_register_prediction(
    model = "decision_tree",
    type = "numeric",
    value = list(
      pre = NULL,
      post = NULL,
      func = c(pkg = "ineqTrees", fun = "ci_predict_parsnip"),
      args = list(
        object = rlang::expr(object$fit),
        newdata = rlang::expr(new_data)
      )
    )
  )

  .ci_register_prediction(
    model = "decision_tree",
    type = "raw",
    value = list(
      pre = NULL,
      post = function(results, object) {
        tibble::tibble(.node = as.integer(results))
      },
      func = c(fun = "predict"),
      args = list(
        object = rlang::expr(object$fit),
        newdata = rlang::expr(new_data),
        type = "node"
      )
    )
  )

  invisible(TRUE)
}

#' @noRd
.onLoad <- function(libname, pkgname) {

}
```

```{r, function-ci_gain}
#' Concentration-index gain for a prediction partition
#'
#' @description
#' Computes the concentration-index impurity reduction from a root partition to
#' groups defined by terminal-node ids or another supplied partition column.
#' This is the yardstick-compatible counterpart to [ci_tree_validation_gain()].
#'
#' @param truth Numeric or logical observed outcomes.
#' @param estimate Numeric predictions. Used as the partition only when `node`
#'   is `NULL`.
#' @param rank Socioeconomic rank values.
#' @param node Optional terminal-node or partition ids. True CI gain requires a
#'   partition; using predictions as a fallback is only an approximation.
#' @param case_weights Optional non-negative case weights.
#' @param type One of `"CI"`, `"CIg"`, `"CIc"`, or `"L"`.
#' @param root_impurity Optional pre-computed root impurity.
#' @param na_rm Should incomplete rows be removed?
#' @param ... Not used.
#'
#' @importFrom yardstick new_numeric_metric
#' @return A numeric concentration-index gain.
#'
#' @export
ci_gain_vec <- function(truth,
                        estimate,
                        rank,
                        node = NULL,
                        case_weights = NULL,
                        type = "CIg",
                        root_impurity = NULL,
                        na_rm = TRUE,
                        ...) {
  truth <- .ci_outcome_numeric(truth, "truth")
  estimate <- as.numeric(estimate)
  rank <- as.numeric(rank)

  if (length(truth) != length(estimate) || length(truth) != length(rank)) {
    stop(
      "`truth`, `estimate`, and `rank` must have the same length.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  case_weights <- .ci_validate_weights(
    case_weights,
    length(truth),
    "case_weights"
  )

  if (is.null(node)) {
    node <- estimate
  }
  if (length(node) != length(truth)) {
    stop("`node` must have the same length as `truth`.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  keep <- stats::complete.cases(truth, estimate, rank, node, case_weights) &
    case_weights > 0

  if (!na_rm && any(!keep)) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  if (!any(keep)) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  truth <- truth[keep]
  rank <- rank[keep]
  node <- node[keep]
  case_weights <- case_weights[keep]

  ci_fun <- ci_factory(type)
  y <- cbind(rank = rank, outcome = truth)

  if (is.null(root_impurity)) {
    root_impurity <- ci_fun(y, case_weights)
  }

  total_weight <- sum(case_weights)
  node_indices <- split(seq_along(truth), node)

  child_impurity <- sum(vapply(
    node_indices,
    function(idx) {
      node_weight <- sum(case_weights[idx])
      (node_weight / total_weight) *
        ci_fun(y[idx, , drop = FALSE], case_weights[idx])
    },
    numeric(1)
  ))

  as.numeric(root_impurity - child_impurity)
}

#' Concentration-index gain metric
#'
#' @param data A data frame.
#' @param ... Arguments passed to methods.
#'
#' @return A yardstick metric tibble.
#'
#' @export
ci_gain <- function(data, ...) {
  UseMethod("ci_gain")
}

ci_gain <- yardstick::new_numeric_metric(ci_gain, direction = "maximize")

#' @export
ci_gain.data.frame <- function(data,
                               truth,
                               estimate,
                               rank,
                               node = NULL,
                               case_weights = NULL,
                               type = "CIg",
                               root_impurity = NULL,
                               na_rm = TRUE,
                               ...) {
  truth <- rlang::enquo(truth)
  estimate <- rlang::enquo(estimate)
  rank <- rlang::enquo(rank)
  node <- rlang::enquo(node)
  case_weights <- rlang::enquo(case_weights)

  truth_vec <- rlang::eval_tidy(truth, data)
  estimate_vec <- rlang::eval_tidy(estimate, data)
  rank_vec <- rlang::eval_tidy(rank, data)

  node_vec <- if (rlang::quo_is_null(node)) {
    NULL
  } else {
    rlang::eval_tidy(node, data)
  }

  weight_vec <- if (rlang::quo_is_null(case_weights)) {
    NULL
  } else {
    rlang::eval_tidy(case_weights, data)
  }

  tibble::tibble(
    .metric = "ci_gain",
    .estimator = "standard",
    .estimate = ci_gain_vec(
      truth = truth_vec,
      estimate = estimate_vec,
      rank = rank_vec,
      node = node_vec,
      case_weights = weight_vec,
      type = type,
      root_impurity = root_impurity,
      na_rm = na_rm
    )
  )
}
```

```{r, function-ci_tuning_metric_set}
#' Create tidymodels tuning metrics for concentration-index model selection
#'
#' @description
#' Builds a yardstick [yardstick::metric_set()] for use in [tune::tune_grid()]
#' with `ineqTrees` parsnip engines. The returned metrics recover the
#' socioeconomic rank and optional case weights from the original analysis data
#' using the `.row` column supplied by `tune_grid()`.
#'
#' Validation gain uses the actual terminal-node IDs carried by the engine's
#' numeric predictions. Forest gain averages the member-tree partition gains;
#' it does not group observations by their averaged predicted risks.
#' Training gain is computed from the fitted analysis sample and carried
#' separately in prediction metadata. It is descriptive training performance,
#' and should not be used to select parameters in place of validation gain.
#' Relative gains divide by the corresponding analysis or assessment root
#' impurity, returning `NA` when that root is numerically zero.
#'
#' @param data Original analysis data used to create the resamples.
#' @param rank_name Name of the socioeconomic rank column in `data`.
#' @param case_weight_name Optional name of the case-weight column in `data`.
#' @param type One of `"CI"`, `"CIg"`, `"CIc"`, or `"L"`.
#' @param metrics Character vector of CI metrics to include. Supported values
#'   are `"validation_gain"`, `"relative_validation_gain"`, `"training_gain"`,
#'   and `"relative_training_gain"`.
#' @param node_name Optional name of a node or partition column. Defaults to
#'   the engine's `.ci_node` column. Supply an explicit column when scoring
#'   manually prepared predictions. Missing partition metadata is an error;
#'   equal predicted risks do not establish equal terminal-node membership.
#'
#' @return A yardstick metric set.
#'
#' @examples
#' if (requireNamespace("yardstick", quietly = TRUE)) {
#'   toy_data <- data.frame(
#'     rank = c(10, 20, 30, 40),
#'     outcome = c(1, 0, 1, 0),
#'     weight = c(1, 1, 2, 2)
#'   )
#'
#'   ci_tuning_metric_set(
#'     toy_data,
#'     rank_name = "rank",
#'     case_weight_name = "weight",
#'     type = "CI",
#'     metrics = c("validation_gain", "relative_validation_gain")
#'   )
#' }
#'
#' @export
ci_tuning_metric_set <- function(data,
                                 rank_name,
                                 case_weight_name = NULL,
                                 type = "CIg",
                                 metrics = c(
                                   "validation_gain",
                                   "relative_validation_gain"
                                 ),
                                 node_name = NULL) {
  data <- as.data.frame(data)
  if (!rank_name %in% names(data)) {
    stop("`data` must contain `rank_name`.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!is.null(case_weight_name) && !case_weight_name %in% names(data)) {
    stop("`data` must contain `case_weight_name`.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  type <- match.arg(type, choices = c("CI", "CIg", "CIc", "L"))
  if (length(type) != 1L) {
    stop("`type` must select exactly one concentration-index criterion.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  allowed_metrics <- c(
    "validation_gain", "relative_validation_gain",
    "training_gain", "relative_training_gain"
  )
  metrics <- match.arg(metrics, allowed_metrics, several.ok = TRUE)
  metrics <- unique(metrics)

  metric_context <- list(
    source_data = data,
    rank_name = rank_name,
    case_weight_name = case_weight_name,
    type = type,
    node_name = node_name
  )

  validation_gain <- function(data, truth, estimate, na_rm = TRUE, ...) {
    .ci_tuning_metric(
      data = data,
      truth = {{ truth }},
      estimate = {{ estimate }},
      context = metric_context,
      metric = "validation_gain",
      na_rm = na_rm
    )
  }
  validation_gain <- yardstick::new_numeric_metric(
    validation_gain,
    direction = "maximize"
  )

  relative_validation_gain <- function(data,
                                       truth,
                                       estimate,
                                       na_rm = TRUE,
                                       ...) {
    .ci_tuning_metric(
      data = data,
      truth = {{ truth }},
      estimate = {{ estimate }},
      context = metric_context,
      metric = "relative_validation_gain",
      na_rm = na_rm
    )
  }
  relative_validation_gain <- yardstick::new_numeric_metric(
    relative_validation_gain,
    direction = "maximize"
  )

  training_gain <- function(data, truth, estimate, na_rm = TRUE, ...) {
    .ci_tuning_metric(
      data = data,
      truth = {{ truth }},
      estimate = {{ estimate }},
      context = metric_context,
      metric = "training_gain",
      na_rm = na_rm
    )
  }
  training_gain <- yardstick::new_numeric_metric(
    training_gain,
    direction = "maximize"
  )

  relative_training_gain <- function(data,
                                     truth,
                                     estimate,
                                     na_rm = TRUE,
                                     ...) {
    .ci_tuning_metric(
      data = data,
      truth = {{ truth }},
      estimate = {{ estimate }},
      context = metric_context,
      metric = "relative_training_gain",
      na_rm = na_rm
    )
  }
  relative_training_gain <- yardstick::new_numeric_metric(
    relative_training_gain,
    direction = "maximize"
  )

  metric_fns <- list(
    validation_gain = validation_gain,
    relative_validation_gain = relative_validation_gain,
    training_gain = training_gain,
    relative_training_gain = relative_training_gain
  )
  do.call(yardstick::metric_set, metric_fns[metrics])
}

#' @noRd
.ci_tuning_vectors <- function(metric_data, context) {
  metric_data <- as.data.frame(metric_data)
  source_data <- context$source_data

  row_id <- NULL
  if (".row" %in% names(metric_data)) {
    row_id <- metric_data$.row
    if (!is.numeric(row_id) || any(!is.finite(row_id)) ||
        any(row_id != floor(row_id)) || any(row_id < 1L) ||
        any(row_id > nrow(source_data))) {
      stop("`.row` must index rows of the original analysis data.",
        call. = FALSE
      )
    }
  }

  if (!is.null(row_id)) {
    rank <- source_data[[context$rank_name]][row_id]
    weights <- if (is.null(context$case_weight_name)) {
      NULL
    } else {
      source_data[[context$case_weight_name]][row_id]
    }
  } else {
    if (!context$rank_name %in% names(metric_data)) {
      stop(
        "CI tuning metrics need `.row` or the rank column in prediction data.",
        call. = FALSE
      )
    }
    rank <- metric_data[[context$rank_name]]
    weights <- if (is.null(context$case_weight_name)) {
      NULL
    } else if (context$case_weight_name %in% names(metric_data)) {
      metric_data[[context$case_weight_name]]
    } else {
      stop(
        "CI tuning metrics need `.row` or the case-weight column in ",
        "prediction data.",
        call. = FALSE
      )
    }
  }

  node_name <- context$node_name
  if (is.null(node_name)) {
    node_name <- ".ci_node"
  }
  if (!node_name %in% names(metric_data)) {
    stop(
      "CI validation gain needs terminal-node metadata. Use ineqTrees ",
      "engine predictions or supply an explicit `node_name`.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  list(rank = rank, weights = weights, node = metric_data[[node_name]])
}

#' Average actual partition gains for a tree or the members of a forest
#' @noRd
.ci_tuning_partition_gain <- function(truth,
                                      estimate,
                                      vectors,
                                      type,
                                      root_impurity,
                                      na_rm) {
  nodes <- vectors$node
  if (is.list(nodes)) {
    member_counts <- lengths(nodes)
    if (!length(nodes) || any(member_counts == 0L) ||
        length(unique(member_counts)) != 1L) {
      stop("Forest node metadata must have one ID per member tree.",
        call. = FALSE
      )
    }
    partitions <- lapply(seq_len(member_counts[1L]), function(member) {
      vapply(nodes, function(row) row[[member]], numeric(1))
    })
  } else {
    partitions <- list(nodes)
  }

  gains <- vapply(partitions, function(partition) {
    ci_gain_vec(
      truth = truth,
      estimate = estimate,
      rank = vectors$rank,
      node = partition,
      case_weights = vectors$weights,
      type = type,
      root_impurity = root_impurity,
      na_rm = na_rm
    )
  }, numeric(1))

  if (all(is.na(gains))) NA_real_ else mean(gains, na.rm = TRUE)
}

#' @noRd
.ci_tuning_root_impurity <- function(truth,
                                     estimate,
                                     rank,
                                     node,
                                     case_weights,
                                     type,
                                     na_rm) {
  truth <- .ci_outcome_numeric(truth, "truth")
  estimate <- as.numeric(estimate)
  rank <- as.numeric(rank)
  case_weights <- .ci_validate_weights(
    case_weights,
    length(truth),
    "case_weights"
  )
  if (is.null(node) || is.list(node)) {
    node <- estimate
  }

  keep <- stats::complete.cases(truth, estimate, rank, node, case_weights) &
    case_weights > 0
  if (!na_rm && any(!keep)) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  if (!any(keep)) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  ci_factory(type)(
    cbind(rank = rank[keep], outcome = truth[keep]),
    case_weights[keep]
  )
}

#' @noRd
.ci_tuning_metric <- function(data,
                              truth,
                              estimate,
                              context,
                              metric = "validation_gain",
                              na_rm = TRUE) {
  truth <- rlang::enquo(truth)
  estimate <- rlang::enquo(estimate)
  grouped_columns <- setdiff(names(attr(data, "groups")), ".rows")
  metric_data <- tibble::as_tibble(data)
  relative <- startsWith(metric, "relative_")

  score_one <- function(metric_data) {
    if (".ci_type" %in% names(metric_data) &&
        !identical(unique(metric_data$.ci_type), context$type)) {
      stop("Metric `type` must match the fitted engine's criterion.",
        call. = FALSE
      )
    }

    if (grepl("training_gain$", metric)) {
      required <- c(".ci_training_gain", ".ci_training_root")
      if (!all(required %in% names(metric_data))) {
        stop("Training gain needs the fitted engine's analysis diagnostics.",
          call. = FALSE
        )
      }
      gain <- unique(metric_data$.ci_training_gain)
      root_impurity <- unique(metric_data$.ci_training_root)
      if (length(gain) != 1L || length(root_impurity) != 1L) {
        stop("Training diagnostics must identify one fitted candidate.",
          call. = FALSE
        )
      }
    } else {
      vectors <- .ci_tuning_vectors(metric_data, context)
      truth_vec <- rlang::eval_tidy(truth, metric_data)
      estimate_vec <- rlang::eval_tidy(estimate, metric_data)

      root_impurity <- NULL
      if (relative) {
        root_impurity <- .ci_tuning_root_impurity(
          truth = truth_vec,
          estimate = estimate_vec,
          rank = vectors$rank,
          node = vectors$node,
          case_weights = vectors$weights,
          type = context$type,
          na_rm = na_rm
        )
      }

      gain <- .ci_tuning_partition_gain(
        truth = truth_vec,
        estimate = estimate_vec,
        vectors = vectors,
        type = context$type,
        root_impurity = root_impurity,
        na_rm = na_rm
      )
    }

    if (relative) {
      if (length(root_impurity) != 1L ||
          is.na(root_impurity) ||
          !is.finite(root_impurity) ||
          abs(root_impurity) <= .Machine$double.eps) {
        gain <- NA_real_
      } else {
        gain <- gain / abs(root_impurity)
      }
    }

    tibble::tibble(
      .metric = metric,
      .estimator = "standard",
      .estimate = gain
    )
  }

  tuning_cols <- intersect(
    c(
      grouped_columns, ".config", "id", "id2",
      "tree_depth", "trees", "mtry", "min_n",
      "min_relative_gain", "min_gain", "minsplit", "minprob", "maxdepth",
      "minbucket", "ntree"
    ),
    names(metric_data)
  )

  if (length(tuning_cols) > 0L) {
    split_key <- do.call(
      interaction,
      c(metric_data[, tuning_cols, drop = FALSE], drop = TRUE, sep = "\r")
    )

    scored <- lapply(split(metric_data, split_key), function(x) {
      out <- score_one(x)
      for (col in tuning_cols) {
        out[[col]] <- x[[col]][[1L]]
      }
      out
    })
    return(tibble::as_tibble(do.call(rbind, scored)))
  }

  score_one(metric_data)
}
```

```{r, function-ci_prediction_index}
#' Concentration index of predictions
#'
#' @description
#' Computes the concentration index of fitted risks or predicted outcomes. This
#' is not split gain, but it is useful for comparing inequality in predictions.
#'
#' @inheritParams ci_gain_vec
#'
#' @return A numeric concentration-index value.
#'
#' @export
ci_prediction_index_vec <- function(estimate,
                                    rank,
                                    case_weights = NULL,
                                    type = "CIg") {
  estimate <- as.numeric(estimate)
  rank <- as.numeric(rank)

  if (length(estimate) != length(rank)) {
    stop("`estimate` and `rank` must have the same length.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  case_weights <- .ci_validate_weights(
    case_weights,
    length(estimate),
    "case_weights"
  )

  keep <- stats::complete.cases(estimate, rank, case_weights) & case_weights > 0
  if (!any(keep)) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  ci_factory(type)(
    cbind(rank = rank[keep], outcome = estimate[keep]),
    case_weights[keep]
  )
}

#' Concentration-index prediction metric
#'
#' @param data A data frame.
#' @param ... Arguments passed to methods.
#'
#' @return A yardstick metric tibble.
#'
#' @export
ci_prediction_index <- function(data, ...) {
  UseMethod("ci_prediction_index")
}

ci_prediction_index <- yardstick::new_numeric_metric(
  ci_prediction_index,
  direction = "maximize"
)

#' @export
ci_prediction_index.data.frame <- function(data,
                                           truth,
                                           estimate,
                                           rank,
                                           case_weights = NULL,
                                           type = "CIg",
                                           ...) {
  estimate <- rlang::enquo(estimate)
  rank <- rlang::enquo(rank)
  case_weights <- rlang::enquo(case_weights)

  estimate_vec <- rlang::eval_tidy(estimate, data)
  rank_vec <- rlang::eval_tidy(rank, data)
  weight_vec <- if (rlang::quo_is_null(case_weights)) {
    NULL
  } else {
    rlang::eval_tidy(case_weights, data)
  }

  tibble::tibble(
    .metric = "ci_prediction_index",
    .estimator = "standard",
    .estimate = ci_prediction_index_vec(
      estimate = estimate_vec,
      rank = rank_vec,
      case_weights = weight_vec,
      type = type
    )
  )
}
```

```{r, tests-tidymodels_bridge}
test_that("parsnip registration refreshes legacy entries without duplicates", {
  exercise_upgrade <- function() {
    registry_names <- paste0(c("decision_tree", "rand_forest"), "_predict")
    original <- lapply(registry_names, parsnip::get_from_env)
    on.exit({
      for (i in seq_along(registry_names)) {
        parsnip::set_env_val(registry_names[i], original[[i]])
      }
    }, add = TRUE)

    for (registry_name in registry_names) {
      registered <- parsnip::get_from_env(registry_name)
      numeric_row <- which(
        registered$engine == "ineqTrees" &
          registered$mode == "regression" & registered$type == "numeric"
      )
      legacy <- list(
        pre = NULL,
        post = function(results, object) {
          tibble::tibble(.pred = as.numeric(results))
        },
        func = c(fun = "predict"),
        args = list(
          object = rlang::expr(object$fit),
          newdata = rlang::expr(new_data),
          type = "response"
        )
      )
      registered$value[[numeric_row]] <- legacy
      parsnip::set_env_val(registry_name, registered)
    }

    expect_silent(register_ineqtrees_parsnip())
    expect_silent(register_ineqtrees_parsnip())

    for (i in seq_along(registry_names)) {
      refreshed <- parsnip::get_from_env(registry_names[i])
      ours <- refreshed$engine == "ineqTrees" &
        refreshed$mode == "regression"
      expect_equal(sort(refreshed$type[ours]), c("numeric", "raw"))
      numeric_value <- refreshed$value[[which(
        ours & refreshed$type == "numeric"
      )]]
      expect_equal(
        numeric_value$func,
        c(pkg = "ineqTrees", fun = "ci_predict_parsnip")
      )
      expect_identical(
        refreshed[refreshed$engine != "ineqTrees", , drop = FALSE],
        original[[i]][original[[i]]$engine != "ineqTrees", , drop = FALSE]
      )
    }
  }

  exercise_upgrade()
})

test_that("decision_tree can fit ci_tree through ineqTrees engine", {
  skip_if_not_installed("parsnip")
  skip_if_not_installed("hardhat")

  register_ineqtrees_parsnip()

  toy_data <- data.frame(
    rank = c(10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80),
    outcome = c(1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1),
    income = c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16),
    group = factor(c("a", "a", "b", "b", "a", "a", "b", "b")),
    weight = 1
  )

  spec <- parsnip::decision_tree(tree_depth = 1, min_n = 1) |>
    parsnip::set_engine(
      "ineqTrees",
      rank_name = "rank",
      outcome_name = "outcome",
      type = "CIg",
      minsplit = 1,
      minprob = 0
    ) |>
    parsnip::set_mode("regression")

  fit <- parsnip::fit(
    spec,
    cbind(rank, outcome) ~ income + group,
    data = toy_data,
    case_weights = hardhat::importance_weights(toy_data$weight)
  )

  expect_s3_class(fit$fit, "ci_tree")

  pred <- predict(fit, new_data = toy_data)
  expect_s3_class(pred, "tbl_df")
  expect_true(".pred" %in% names(pred))
  expect_equal(nrow(pred), nrow(toy_data))

  nodes <- predict(fit, new_data = toy_data, type = "raw")
  expect_type(nodes, "integer")
  expect_equal(length(nodes), nrow(toy_data))
})

  expect_equal(nrow(nodes), nrow(toy_data))
})

test_that("rand_forest engine passes min_relative_gain to control", {
  skip_if_not_installed("parsnip")

  register_ineqtrees_parsnip()

  toy_data <- data.frame(
    rank = c(10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80),
    outcome = c(1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1),
    income = c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16)
  )

  spec <- parsnip::rand_forest(trees = 3, min_n = 1) |>
    parsnip::set_engine(
      "ineqTrees",
      rank_name = "rank",
      outcome_name = "outcome",
      minsplit = 1,
      minprob = 0,
      maxdepth = 1,
      min_relative_gain = 0.25
    ) |>
    parsnip::set_mode("regression")

  fit <- parsnip::fit(
    spec,
    cbind(rank, outcome) ~ income,
    data = toy_data
  )

  expect_equal(fit$fit$control$min_relative_gain, 0.25)
})

test_that("ci_gain computes a yardstick-style metric", {
  toy_pred <- data.frame(
    truth = c(1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1),
    pred = c(0.8, 0.2, 0.7, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9),

    node = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2),
    weight = 1
  )

  out <- ci_gain(
    toy_pred,
    truth = truth,
    estimate = pred,
    rank = rank,
    node = node,
    case_weights = weight,
    type = "CIg"
  )

  expect_s3_class(out, "tbl_df")
  expect_equal(out$.metric, "ci_gain")
  expect_true(is.finite(out$.estimate))
})

test_that("ci_gain_vec rejects non-finite case weights", {
  truth <- c(1, 0, 1)
  estimate <- c(0.8, 0.2, 0.7)
  rank <- c(10, 20, 30)

  for (bad_weights in list(c(1, Inf, 1), c(1, NaN, 1), c(1, -Inf, 1))) {
    expect_error(
      ci_gain_vec(
        truth = truth,
        estimate = estimate,
        rank = rank,
        node = node,

      ),

    )

})

test_that("CI tuning metrics recover ranks and weights from .row", {
  source_data <- data.frame(
    rank = c(10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60),
    outcome = c(1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1),
    weight = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2)
  )
  pred_data <- data.frame(
    .row = 1:6,
    truth = source_data$outcome,
    pred = c(0.8, 0.2, 0.7, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9),
    .ci_node = c(1L, 2L, 1L, 2L, 1L, 1L)
  )

  metrics <- ci_tuning_metric_set(
    source_data,
    rank_name = "rank",
    case_weight_name = "weight",
    type = "CI",
    metrics = c("validation_gain", "relative_validation_gain")
  )

  out <- metrics(pred_data, truth = truth, estimate = pred)
  root_impurity <- ci_factory("CI")(
    cbind(rank = source_data$rank, outcome = source_data$outcome),
    source_data$weight
  )

  expect_s3_class(out, "tbl_df")
  expect_equal(out$.metric, c("validation_gain", "relative_validation_gain"))
  expect_true(all(is.finite(out$.estimate)))
  expect_equal(
    out$.estimate[out$.metric == "relative_validation_gain"],
    out$.estimate[out$.metric == "validation_gain"] / abs(root_impurity)
  )
})

test_that("ci_tuning_metric_set preserves tuning columns for tune_grid joins", {
  source_data <- data.frame(
    rank = c(10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60),
    outcome = c(1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1),
    weight = 1
  )
  pred_data <- rbind(
    data.frame(
      .row = 1:6,
      truth = source_data$outcome,
      pred = c(0.8, 0.2, 0.7, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9),
      .ci_node = c(1L, 2L, 1L, 2L, 1L, 1L),
      min_relative_gain = 0,
      .config = "config_1"
    ),
    data.frame(
      .row = 1:6,
      truth = source_data$outcome,
      pred = c(0.9, 0.1, 0.6, 0.4, 0.7, 0.8),
      .ci_node = c(1L, 2L, 1L, 2L, 1L, 1L),
      min_relative_gain = 0.25,
      .config = "config_2"
    )
  )

  metrics <- ci_tuning_metric_set(
    source_data,
    rank_name = "rank",
    case_weight_name = "weight",
    type = "CI",
    metrics = "validation_gain"
  )

  out <- metrics(pred_data, truth = truth, estimate = pred)

  expect_equal(nrow(out), 2L)
  expect_true(all(c("min_relative_gain", ".config") %in% names(out)))
  expect_equal(out$min_relative_gain, c(0, 0.25))
  expect_equal(out$.config, c("config_1", "config_2"))
})

test_that("CI tuning keeps distinct leaves with equal predicted risks", {
  source_data <- data.frame(
    rank = 1:8,
    truth = rep(c(0, 0, 1, 1), 2)
  )
  predictions <- data.frame(
    .row = 1:8,
    truth = source_data$truth,
    .pred = 0.5,
    .ci_node = rep(1:2, each = 4)
  )
  metrics <- ci_tuning_metric_set(source_data, "rank", type = "CI")
  scores <- metrics(predictions, truth = truth, estimate = .pred)

  # Root impurity is 1/4; each leaf has impurity 1/2.
  expect_equal(scores$.estimate, c(-0.25, -1))

  predictions$.ci_node <- NULL
  expect_error(
    metrics(predictions, truth = truth, estimate = .pred),
    "terminal-node metadata"
  )
})

test_that("CI tuning rejects invalid row mapping and criterion mismatches", {
  source_data <- data.frame(rank = 1:4, truth = c(0, 1, 0, 1))
  predictions <- data.frame(
    .row = c(1, 2, 3, 4.5),
    truth = source_data$truth,
    .pred = 0.5,
    .ci_node = 1L
  )
  metrics <- ci_tuning_metric_set(source_data, "rank", type = "CI")
  expect_error(
    metrics(predictions, truth = truth, estimate = .pred),
    "original analysis data"
  )

  predictions$.row <- 1:4
  predictions$.ci_type <- "CIg"
  expect_error(
    metrics(predictions, truth = truth, estimate = .pred),
    "must match"
  )
})

test_that("relative gains are missing for zero roots", {
  source_data <- data.frame(rank = 1:4, truth = 1)
  predictions <- data.frame(
    .row = 1:4,
    truth = 1,
    .pred = 1,
    .ci_node = 1L,
    .ci_type = "CI",
    .ci_training_gain = 0,
    .ci_training_root = 0
  )
  metric_names <- c(
    "validation_gain", "relative_validation_gain",
    "training_gain", "relative_training_gain"
  )
  metrics <- ci_tuning_metric_set(
    source_data, "rank", type = "CI", metrics = metric_names
  )
  scores <- metrics(predictions, truth = truth, estimate = .pred)
  expect_equal(scores$.estimate, c(0, NA_real_, 0, NA_real_))

  predictions$truth <- c(0, 0, 1, 1)
  changed <- metrics(predictions, truth = truth, estimate = .pred)
  expect_equal(changed$.estimate[3:4], scores$.estimate[3:4])
})

test_that("tune_grid reports fitted analysis and assessment gains", {
  skip_if_not_installed("tune")
  skip_if_not_installed("workflows")
  skip_if_not_installed("rsample")
  skip_if_not_installed("hardhat")

  set.seed(302)
  analysis_data <- data.frame(
    rank = rep(1:24, each = 2),
    outcome = rbinom(48, 1, seq(0.1, 0.85, length.out = 48)),
    predictor = rep(seq_len(8), 6),
    group = factor(rep(letters[1:3], each = 16)),
    weight = rep(c(1, 2, 5, 0), 12)
  )
  analysis_data$case_wt <- hardhat::importance_weights(analysis_data$weight)
  folds <- rsample::vfold_cv(analysis_data, v = 3)
  metric_names <- c(
    "validation_gain", "relative_validation_gain",
    "training_gain", "relative_training_gain"
  )

  for (model in c("tree", "forest")) {
    for (criterion in c("CI", "CIg", "CIc", "L")) {
      specification <- if (model == "tree") {
        parsnip::decision_tree(
          tree_depth = tune::tune(id = "depth"), min_n = 3
        )
      } else {
        parsnip::rand_forest(trees = 3, mtry = 2, min_n = tune::tune())
      }
      specification <- parsnip::set_engine(
        specification,
        "ineqTrees",
        rank_name = "rank",
        outcome_name = "outcome",
        type = criterion,
        minsplit = 6,
        minprob = 0
      )
      specification <- parsnip::set_mode(specification, "regression")
      model_workflow <- workflows::workflow()
      model_workflow <- workflows::add_model(model_workflow, specification)
      model_workflow <- workflows::add_formula(
        model_workflow, outcome ~ rank + predictor + group
      )
      model_workflow <- workflows::add_case_weights(model_workflow, case_wt)
      grid <- if (model == "tree") {
        data.frame(depth = c(1L, 2L))
      } else {
        data.frame(min_n = c(3L, 8L))
      }
      metrics <- ci_tuning_metric_set(
        analysis_data,
        rank_name = "rank",
        case_weight_name = "weight",
        type = criterion,
        metrics = metric_names
      )
      set.seed(714)
      tuned <- tune::tune_grid(
        model_workflow,
        resamples = folds,
        grid = grid,
        metrics = metrics,
        control = tune::control_grid(
          allow_par = FALSE,
          save_pred = TRUE,
          extract = workflows::extract_fit_engine
        )
      )
      scores <- tune::collect_metrics(tuned, summarize = FALSE)
      expect_equal(nrow(tune::collect_notes(tuned)), 0L)
      expect_equal(nrow(scores), 24L)

      rescored <- metrics(
        tune::collect_predictions(tuned), truth = outcome, estimate = .pred
      )
      score_keys <- paste(scores$id, scores$.config, scores$.metric)
      rescored_keys <- paste(rescored$id, rescored$.config, rescored$.metric)
      expect_equal(nrow(rescored), nrow(scores))
      expect_equal(
        rescored$.estimate[match(score_keys, rescored_keys)],
        scores$.estimate
      )

      for (fold in seq_len(nrow(folds))) {
        training <- rsample::analysis(folds$splits[[fold]])
        assessment <- rsample::assessment(folds$splits[[fold]])
        extracted <- tuned$.extracts[[fold]]
        for (candidate in seq_len(nrow(extracted))) {
          fit <- extracted$.extracts[[candidate]]
          saved <- tune::collect_predictions(tuned)
          saved <- saved[
            saved$id == folds$id[fold] &
              saved$.config == extracted$.config[candidate],
          ]
          samples <- list(assessment, training)
          partitions <- list(
            saved$.ci_node,
            attr(fit, "ci_training_diagnostics")$nodes
          )
          expected <- vapply(seq_along(samples), function(sample_id) {
            sample <- samples[[sample_id]]
            nodes <- partitions[[sample_id]]
            if (is.list(nodes)) {
              nodes <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, nodes))
            } else {
              nodes <- data.frame(node = nodes)
            }
            mean(vapply(nodes, function(member_nodes) {
              ci_gain_vec(
                sample$outcome,
                estimate = sample$outcome,
                rank = sample$rank,
                node = member_nodes,
                case_weights = sample$weight,
                type = criterion
              )
            }, numeric(1)))
          }, numeric(1))
          roots <- vapply(list(assessment, training), function(sample) {
            ci_factory(criterion)(
              cbind(sample$rank, sample$outcome), sample$weight
            )
          }, numeric(1))
          relative <- ifelse(
            abs(roots) <= .Machine$double.eps, NA_real_, expected / roots
          )
          selected <- scores$id == folds$id[fold] &
            scores$.config == extracted$.config[candidate]
          actual <- scores[selected, ]

          expect_equal(
            actual$.estimate[match(metric_names, actual$.metric)],
            c(expected[1], relative[1], expected[2], relative[2]),
            tolerance = 1e-12,
            info = paste(model, criterion, fold, candidate)
          )
        }
      }

      best <- tune::select_best(tuned, metric = "validation_gain")
      final_workflow <- tune::finalize_workflow(model_workflow, best)
      final_fit <- parsnip::fit(final_workflow, data = analysis_data)
      prediction <- predict(final_fit, new_data = analysis_data)
      engine <- workflows::extract_fit_engine(final_fit)
      expect_equal(
        prediction$.pred,
        as.numeric(predict(engine, newdata = analysis_data))
      )
    }
  }
})
```

## Example usage

```{r example, eval=FALSE}
library(ineqTrees)
library(parsnip)
library(hardhat)

register_ineqtrees_parsnip()

tree_spec <- decision_tree(tree_depth = 4, min_n = 100) |>
  set_engine(
    "ineqTrees",
    rank_name = "wealth",
    outcome_name = "deadu5_num",
    type = "CIg",
    minsplit = 500,
    minprob = 0.01,
    min_gain = 0.001
  ) |>
  set_mode("regression")

tree_fit <- fit(
  tree_spec,
  cbind(wealth, deadu5_num) ~ rural + male + reg,
  data = congo_model_dt,
  case_weights = hardhat::importance_weights(congo_model_dt$sample_weight)
)

predict(tree_fit, new_data = congo_model_dt)
predict(tree_fit, new_data = congo_model_dt, type = "raw")

forest_spec <- rand_forest(trees = 500, mtry = 4, min_n = 100) |>
  set_engine(
    "ineqTrees",
    rank_name = "wealth",
    outcome_name = "deadu5_num",
    type = "CIg",
    minsplit = 500,
    minprob = 0.01,
    maxdepth = 5,
    min_gain = 0.001,
    perturb = list(replace = FALSE, fraction = 0.632)
  ) |>
  set_mode("regression")

forest_fit <- fit(
  forest_spec,
  cbind(wealth, deadu5_num) ~ rural + male + reg,
  data = congo_model_dt,
  case_weights = hardhat::importance_weights(congo_model_dt$sample_weight)
)

predict(forest_fit, new_data = congo_model_dt)
```
